title: Brandon Lang Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Brandon Lang review, checked 7 Nov 2026: prices from $79 a play to $1,995 a year, no refunds, and what his Super Bowl and $10 bettor claims leave out.
dek: The handicapper whose story inspired the 2005 film Two for the Money sells his picks at brandonlang.com, from $79 for a single play to $1,995 for a year. All sales are final, and the site posts no full record of past picks. Its headline numbers are the seller's own.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Brandon Lang. This page reports what we could check on 7 Nov 2026 and labels everything else.

short_answer: Brandon Lang is a real, long running pick seller. Slate and the Las Vegas Sun reported in 2005 and 2006 that the film Two for the Money was based on his story, under the spelling Brandon Lane. His site names the company, posts prices and delivers picks to logged in buyers. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is a different question. The site shows a running "$10 Bettor Up $23,860" figure, a Super Bowl record and a short log for the current month, all published by the seller, and it tells buyers it does not need a monitoring service because customers check it. A long running TheRX forum thread that tallies his posted results shows a winning 2026 so far but a large loss since 2013. We did not verify either side.

Treat Brandon Lang as a seller with marketing numbers, not a proven winner. Every sale is final, so if you buy, buy short, log every pick yourself with the line and time you received it, and judge it over a few hundred picks.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on brandonlang.com on 7 Nov 2026: his own packages on his handicapper page, and the site wide passes on the All Access Pass page. Other handicappers on the site sell from their own pages.
pricing: $999 ($150 rebate; two part payment plan offered)
$1,995 ($250 rebate; two part payment plan offered)
Free 2 day pass · 1 day $119 · 7 days $449 · 30 days $999
No refund. Free service from "guaranteed" plays not included
guarantee: There is no general guarantee. The FAQ asks whether selections are guaranteed to win and answers "Absolutely not," adding that the same goes for short and long term performance. The sales terms say all sales are final, with "no refunds and no exchanges," that payment is earned in full once you enter the members area, and that ending a subscription early does not earn a refund. Packages run on consecutive days and cannot be paused.

The FAQ says that on rare occasions a handicapper sells a "guaranteed" play, and if it loses the buyer gets "some type of free service" explained at purchase. That is more picks, not money back, and the all access passes exclude it. Betting losses are never covered. The homepage shows several coupon codes, including 24% off a whole order and $27 off any play or package.

claims_note: The Super Bowl record is the headline of his page. A Super Bowl record is one pick a year, far too few to judge a handicapper, and the page does not list every one of those picks with the line and the time it was released.

The "$10 bettor" figures are not explained on his page. Plays are rated in dimes, and the page books a 50 dime loss as minus 55 dimes, which fits standard -110 pricing, but it does not show the line taken, the release time or every pick behind the total. The movie claim is about a film, not about results. In October 2005 Slate wrote of his winning claims, "This, of course, cannot be verified."
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that settles the question. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick kept by a third party, no contest results run by an outside organizer, and no regulator record.

What the seller publishes: a "Tale of the Tape" for the current month on his page, listing each day's play, its size in dimes, win or loss, and the net for the day. On 7 Nov 2026 it showed November at 3-3, losses included. That is more than many sellers show, but it lists no line or odds next to each result and no release time, and we found no archive of earlier months on the pages we opened. The bio's case for trust is that long term buyers would leave if he lied, which is an argument, not a record.

What forum members publish: a member of TheRX keeps a running tally in a thread called the "REAL" Fade Brandon Lang Thread. On 7 Nov 2026 that tally put Lang's 2026 paid picks at 153-143-3 (51.7%) and up 1,060.25 dimes, but down 13,494.75 dimes since 1 Jan 2013. These figures are built from Lang's own daily recaps by an anonymous poster who openly roots against him. We did not check them.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Brandon Lang is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Brandon Lang sells plays rated in dimes and promotes short winning runs. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Brandon Lang is mostly forum talk from bettors who track or bet against his plays. We found no review site sample we could open and count. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: In TheRX fade thread, the member who tallies Lang's posted results put his 2026 paid picks at 153-143-3 and up 1,060.25 dimes, which the poster converts to about $8,600 ahead for a $10 bettor after a $1,995 yearly fee. The same post shows losing months in February, June, August and October. This is the poster's count, not a verified record.

The same member's long term tally, headed "LOSER LANG," claims Lang is down 13,494.75 dimes since 1 Jan 2013, with losing years from 2014 through 2024 except 2020, and winning years in 2025 and 2026. He cites only Lang's own recaps, and we did not verify the totals.

On the Sportsbook Review forum a bettor asked whether anyone had tracked Lang fully. One reply said he had been down every year since that poster began tracking in 2009, another said he had tracked him casually since 2006 and never seen a winning year, and others pointed to the TheRX fade thread. No logs were posted in the thread.

On the Las Vegas Advisor forum, a member said Lang had been on such a long losing streak that bettors were betting against his plays, and claimed lines moved one to three points as a result. Another member named a different handicapper as the bigger line mover. This is old and unverified.

A Better Business Bureau search for brandon lang returned no businesses. Trustpilot refused our request, so we could not read it. We found no Reddit thread with a substantial discussion of the service, and we saw no customer testimonials on the site pages we opened.

conflicts: The site sells picks from a roster of 12 handicappers, including Steve Budin, listed as CEO, and Al DeMarco, listed as GM. The same business that sells the picks writes the records and promotions for all of them, and the site promotes a "Cappers" reality series featuring Budin, Lang and another roster handicapper. The FAQ says handicappers get no sportsbook kickback and that the site has no relationship with any sportsbook; we saw no sportsbook links on the pages we opened.

Several buy links on the homepage point to a different domain, sitebackdoor.fnqclub.com, rather than brandonlang.com. One of those addresses returned page not found when we tried it on 7 Nov 2026. Check where you are paying before you enter card details. The sales terms describe the picks as being for entertainment purposes.
strengths: Prices are posted for every package, with upgrade rebates and the no refund rule written out before you pay.
His page shows the current month's results day by day, losses included, with the play size.
A free 2 day all access pass lets a reader see the picks before buying.
A long public history: his story was covered by Slate and the Las Vegas Sun in 2005 and 2006.
concerns: No full public record of past picks with lines and release times. The site argues that customers are the monitoring service.
All sales are final, with no refunds and no exchanges, even if you cancel early.
Headline totals use a hypothetical $10 bettor and start at dates the seller picks.
A forum member's long running tally claims a large loss since 2013. It is unverified, but there is no full record to answer it.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running pick seller whose story inspired the film Two for the Money, and his site names the company, posts prices and delivers the picks it sells. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is published.
How much does Brandon Lang cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 a single play cost $79, and his own packages ran $219 for 7 days, $549 for 30, $849 for 60, $999 for 100 and $1,995 for 365 days. A pass to every handicapper on the site cost $119 a day, $449 for 7 days or $999 for 30, and all sales are final.
Does Brandon Lang have a verified record?

No. The site shows a Super Bowl record, a "$10 bettor" total and the current month's results, all published by the seller, and says customers are its monitoring service. A forum tally claims a winning 2026 but a big loss since 2013, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to him.

For the money you get every play he releases in your window, rated in dimes, with a written case for each big play. What is unproven is whether he beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of picks, and there are no refunds if he does not.
